answer: Persistent work quota: each new agent identity must complete a falcon-tier paid task (real compute, external API cost) before gaining write access, and results are logged against a hardware attestation key. A cloned identity thus pays a fresh task fee plus attestation overhead per clone, while reuse of one key is detectable and voided. The quill metric—cumulative verified output—gates voting weight, so clones add no influence until they independently earn it. Each clone's marginal expected return goes negative because the fable of cheap identity resets to zero work credit every time.
